-- ── Constants (ref-lua l.1-2) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Globals, as the reference declares them: NUM_FACTIONS_DISPLAYED is the row-slot count the -- XML below instantiates, REPUTATIONFRAME_FACTIONHEIGHT the faux kit's pixel value step. NUM_FACTIONS_DISPLAYED = 15 REPUTATIONFRAME_FACTIONHEIGHT = 26
-- ── GlobalStrings (ref-GlobalStrings.lua, cited per line) ─────────────────────────────── -- The `X = X or "..."` idiom is this codebase's convention: the app runs the real localized -- GlobalStrings.lua off the patch chain BEFORE any window file, so the installed locale -- wins and these copies only fill in for the test harnesses, which load no chain. FACTION = FACTION or "Faction" -- :1938 STANDING = STANDING or "Standing" -- :4193 AT_WAR = AT_WAR or "At War" -- :77 MOVE_TO_INACTIVE = MOVE_TO_INACTIVE or "Move to Inactive" -- :2706 SHOW_FACTION_ON_MAINSCREEN = SHOW_FACTION_ON_MAINSCREEN or "Show as Experience Bar" -- :3438 REPUTATION_FACTION_DESCRIPTION = REPUTATION_FACTION_DESCRIPTION or "These are the factions that you have interacted with." -- :3330 REPUTATION_STANDING_DESCRIPTION = REPUTATION_STANDING_DESCRIPTION or "The further to the right your standing bar is the closer you are to improving your reputation to the next tier with that faction. The Standing Levels in order are Hated, Hostile, Unfriendly, Neutral, Friendly, Honored, Revered and Exalted." -- :3331 REPUTATION_STATUS_AT_WAR = REPUTATION_STATUS_AT_WAR or "You are currently at war with this group." -- :3333 REPUTATION_AT_WAR_DESCRIPTION = REPUTATION_AT_WAR_DESCRIPTION or "This determines how you will interact with members of this faction. If you have at war checked then your default behavior will be to attack them. If you do not have it checked you will not be able to attack them. " -- :3329
-- The two SYNTHETIC header names. The engine reads these globals out of the VM itself -- (reputation.rs `synthetic_header`), which is the only reason either string has a consumer -- at all: GlobalStrings.lua defines both and no reference FrameXML file anywhere reads -- them, because the real client builds the list C-side. `FACTION_OTHER` heads the -- parentless bucket (key 0); `FACTION_INACTIVE` heads the bucket a faction moves to when -- the popup's "Move to Inactive" box is ticked (key -1), which the engine folds by default -- on every rebuild, exactly as the client does. FACTION_OTHER = FACTION_OTHER or "Other" -- :1943 FACTION_INACTIVE = FACTION_INACTIVE or "Inactive" -- :1942
-- The eight standing names, and their `_FEMALE` twins (:1947-1962). enUS spells both the -- same; a localized client's own GlobalStrings.lua overwrites the pair and the gender rule -- in BenillaReputation_StandingLabel starts mattering. FACTION_STANDING_LABEL1 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL1 or "Hated" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL2 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL2 or "Hostile" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL3 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL3 or "Unfriendly" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL4 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL4 or "Neutral" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL5 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL5 or "Friendly" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL6 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL6 or "Honored" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL7 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL7 or "Revered" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL8 = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL8 or "Exalted" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL1_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL1_FEMALE or "Hated" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL2_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL2_FEMALE or "Hostile" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL3_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL3_FEMALE or "Unfriendly" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL4_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL4_FEMALE or "Neutral" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL5_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL5_FEMALE or "Friendly" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL6_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL6_FEMALE or "Honored" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL7_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL7_FEMALE or "Revered" FACTION_STANDING_LABEL8_FEMALE = FACTION_STANDING_LABEL8_FEMALE or "Exalted"
-- `FACTION_BAR_COLORS` (ref-lua l.3-12) is NOT declared here: it lives in ActionBar.xml -- beside `ReputationWatchBar_Update`, its other consumer, because that file must be able to -- index it with no reputation file loaded and this one cannot be loaded without it (this -- file's header comment, deviation 1). ActionBar.xml is manifest entry 94 against this -- file's 213, so the table is always there by the time a row paints.
-- The standing name for `standingID` (1..8) at the player's gender — the reference's -- `GetText("FACTION_STANDING_LABEL"..standingID, gender)` (ref-lua l.65) with its C-side -- lookup collapsed (this file's header comment, deviation 2). `UnitSex` answers 2 for male -- and 3 for female, which is the value the reference passes straight through. function BenillaReputation_StandingLabel(standingID, gender) if gender == 3 then local female = getglobal("FACTION_STANDING_LABEL" .. standingID .. "_FEMALE") if female then return female end end return getglobal("FACTION_STANDING_LABEL" .. standingID) or "" end
-- A checkbox takes the client's 1/nil rather than a boolean, and every box on this page is -- driven straight off a flag out of the faction tuple — so one verb, not an if/else pair -- per box. function BenillaReputation_SetBoxChecked(box, on) box:SetChecked(on and 1 or nil) end
-- The selection glow is a PAIR of textures, because the row's frame art is two pieces -- (`$parentHighlight1` reaches back over the name, `2` caps the bar's right end). They are -- always raised and dropped together, from three places: the update below, and the row's -- own OnEnter/OnLeave. function BenillaReputationBar_SetGlow(barName, lit) local left, right = getglobal(barName .. "Highlight1"), getglobal(barName .. "Highlight2") if lit then left:Show() right:Show() else left:Hide() right:Hide() end end
-- Fill the detail popup for the row at `factionIndex` (ref-lua l.106-133 is the -- specification). Called only when the popup is up AND this row is the selected one. -- Everything it touches is a `ReputationDetail*` widget, which is the addon-visible name -- and so not ours to vary; what IS ours is that the three tick states are one verb and the -- at-war label's colour is written once instead of once per arm. function BenillaReputationDetail_Fill(factionIndex, name, description, atWarWith, canToggleAtWar, isWatched) ReputationDetailFactionName:SetText(name) ReputationDetailFactionDescription:SetText(description) BenillaReputation_SetBoxChecked(ReputationDetailAtWarCheckBox, atWarWith) -- A peace-forced faction cannot be fought, so its box is dead and the label greys off -- the angry red to say so. local label = GRAY_FONT_COLOR if canToggleAtWar then label = RED_FONT_COLOR ReputationDetailAtWarCheckBox:Enable() else ReputationDetailAtWarCheckBox:Disable() end ReputationDetailAtWarCheckBoxText:SetTextColor(label.r, label.g, label.b) BenillaReputation_SetBoxChecked(ReputationDetailInactiveCheckBox, IsFactionInactive(factionIndex)) BenillaReputation_SetBoxChecked(ReputationDetailMainScreenCheckBox, isWatched) end
-- A row SLOT is a pair of twins on one line — the header BUTTON `ReputationHeader<i>` and -- the faction STATUSBAR `ReputationBar<i>` with all its furniture — of which exactly one is -- ever up. The two verbs below cover every state a slot can be in (a header, a faction, or -- nothing at all), and each raises the twin it wants and drops the other, so no caller has -- to remember the pairing.
-- Slot `i` has nothing to hold: both twins go dark (ref-lua l.141-143). function BenillaReputationSlot_Clear(i) getglobal("ReputationHeader" .. i):Hide() getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i):Hide() end
-- Slot `i` holds the visible row at `factionIndex`. Split out of the update loop so that -- loop is about the SCROLL WINDOW and this is about ONE ROW; the eleven-wide faction tuple -- then has exactly one reader in the file. ref-lua l.51-139 is the specification, and the -- reference's own unread `rightBarTexture` local is not carried (this file's header -- comment, deviation 6). function BenillaReputationSlot_Paint(i, factionIndex, gender) local bar = getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i) local header = getglobal("ReputationHeader" .. i) local check = getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i .. "Check") local name, description, standingID, barMin, barMax, barValue, atWarWith, canToggleAtWar, isHeader, isCollapsed, isWatched = GetFactionInfo(factionIndex)
if isHeader then -- A GROUP HEADER: the group's name, the fold icon its state calls for, and the -- visible index a click on it folds by. The icon says what the click WILL do — an -- open group offers the minus that shuts it, a shut one the plus that opens it. local foldIcon = "Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MinusButton-Up" if isCollapsed then foldIcon = "Interface\\Buttons\\UI-PlusButton-Up" end header.index = factionIndex header.isCollapsed = isCollapsed header:SetText(name) header:SetNormalTexture(foldIcon) header:Show() bar:Hide() check:Hide() return end
-- A FACTION: the name and the standing word it currently wears. local standingText = BenillaReputation_StandingLabel(standingID, gender) local factionName = getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i .. "FactionName") factionName:SetText(name) getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i .. "FactionStanding"):SetText(standingText)
-- The crossed-swords pennant off the row's right end. local atWarIndicator = getglobal("ReputationBar" .. i .. "AtWarCheck") if atWarWith then atWarIndicator:Show() else atWarIndicator:Hide() end
-- The engine hands the rank window over ABSOLUTE for exactly this reason: -- reputation.rs's module doc names the reference's own normalization (ref-lua l.79-82) -- as the contract the tuple is written against. The bar's range is the window's WIDTH, -- its value the distance into it, and the hover tooltip is the same pair spelled out. local rankWidth = barMax - barMin local progress = barValue - barMin bar.id = factionIndex bar.standingText = standingText bar.tooltip = HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR_CODE .. " " .. progress .. " / " .. rankWidth .. FONT_COLOR_CODE_CLOSE bar:SetMinMaxValues(0, rankWidth) bar:SetValue(progress) -- UNGUARDED, deliberately, exactly as the reference has it (ref-lua l.89). -- `GetFactionInfo` is eleven wide on EVERY path including a miss, and its miss puts the -- client's own `1` in the standingID slot for precisely this index (reputation.rs -- `unknown_faction`) — so the caller's `factionIndex <= numFactions` gate is belt, and -- that `1` is braces. Adding a nil-check here would be inventing a branch the client -- does not have and cannot reach. local color = FACTION_BAR_COLORS[standingID] bar:SetStatusBarColor(color.r, color.g, color.b) bar:SetID(factionIndex) bar:Show() header:Hide()
-- The watched checkmark rides the END of the name string, so the name box gives up 10 -- of its 110px to make room for it (ref-lua l.95-103). if isWatched then check:Show() factionName:SetWidth(100) check:SetPoint("LEFT", factionName, "LEFT", factionName:GetStringWidth(), 0) else check:Hide() factionName:SetWidth(110) end
-- The selected row keeps its glow with the mouse away, and is the one that fills the -- popup while the popup is open (ref-lua l.105-139). local selected = factionIndex == GetSelectedFaction() if selected and ReputationDetailFrame:IsShown() then BenillaReputationDetail_Fill(factionIndex, name, description, atWarWith, canToggleAtWar, isWatched) end BenillaReputationBar_SetGlow("ReputationBar" .. i, selected) end
-- The list page (ref-lua ReputationFrame_Update, l.32-149 is the specification): fit the -- scroll window to the list, then bind each of the fixed slots to the row the offset puts -- under it, on the house faux-scroll kit rather than the reference's real ScrollFrame -- (this file's header comment, deviation 4). function ReputationFrame_Update() local numFactions = GetNumFactions() local scrollFrame = getglobal("ReputationListScrollFrame")
-- ref-lua l.39-41. The reset is a no-op in every reachable case — FauxScrollFrame_Update -- has already clamped `frame.offset` to 0 when the list fits and seated the bar at -- `offset * valueStep`, so this SetValue writes the value the Slider already holds and -- its change-gate (decision 0250) drops it before it could re-enter this function. -- Kept because it is the reference's line, not because it does anything. local showBar = FauxScrollFrame_Update(scrollFrame, numFactions, NUM_FACTIONS_DISPLAYED, REPUTATIONFRAME_FACTIONHEIGHT) -- Our trough is not the reference's business: it follows the bar the ref just decided -- about (1860). BenillaScrollTrough_Follow("ReputationListScrollFrame") if not showBar then getglobal("ReputationListScrollFrameScrollBar"):SetValue(0) end local factionOffset = FauxScrollFrame_GetOffset(scrollFrame)
local gender = UnitSex("player") for i = 1, NUM_FACTIONS_DISPLAYED do local factionIndex = factionOffset + i if factionIndex <= numFactions then BenillaReputationSlot_Paint(i, factionIndex, gender) else BenillaReputationSlot_Clear(i) end end -- ref-lua l.146-148: nothing selected means nothing to detail. `GetSelectedFaction` -- answers 0 both for "never selected" and for "the selected faction is folded away -- under a collapsed header" (reputation.rs), so a fold closes the popup too. if GetSelectedFaction() == 0 then ReputationDetailFrame:Hide() end end
-- A bar click toggles the popup for that faction (ref-lua ReputationBar_OnClick, -- l.151-159): the row that is already showing shuts it, any other row moves the selection -- and opens it. Parameterless and reading `this`, exactly as the reference writes it: our -- dispatcher sets `this` before invoking a handler (script/event.rs `invoke_with_globals`) -- and it stays set through the call, the same contract ScrollTemplates.xml's -- `FauxScrollFrame_OnVerticalScroll` already relies on. function ReputationBar_OnClick() if ReputationDetailFrame:IsShown() and GetSelectedFaction() == this.id then ReputationDetailFrame:Hide() return end SetSelectedFaction(this.id) ReputationDetailFrame:Show() ReputationFrame_Update() end
-- A header click folds or unfolds its group (ref l.9-15, the template's own OnClick). -- THE ADDED LINE is the repaint: the reference's `Collapse`/`ExpandFactionHeader` are C -- bindings that raise UPDATE_FACTION on their way out, ours are pure model writes (this -- file's header comment, deviation 3) — SkillFrame.xml's `BenillaSkillTypeLabel_OnClick` -- carries the identical addition for the identical reason. -- -- `header.index` is the slot's own VISIBLE row index, stamped by the update loop that last -- painted it, and it must stay that: an index that is not a header — `0`, a bar row, a stale -- one past the end — folds or unfolds EVERY header instead (the client's own fall-through at -- `0x4d6a50`/`0x4d6aa0`, which reputation.rs reproduces). Nothing here can reach that arm, -- because a slot only ever shows its header twin while the loop has just written a header -- index into it; the note is here so a future edit does not reach it by accident. function BenillaReputationHeader_OnClick(header) if header.isCollapsed then ExpandFactionHeader(header.index) else CollapseFactionHeader(header.index) end ReputationFrame_Update() end
-- The popup's three boxes (ref l.758-766, l.810-818, l.839-848). The at-war box is the -- reference's own body unchanged — it already repaints. The inactive box gains the added -- repaint (this file's header comment, deviation 3): its flip re-parents the row under the -- "Inactive" header there and then, so the list on screen is stale the moment it returns. -- The main-screen box gets NO addition — see the same note for why the round trip, not a -- repaint, is what moves the watched checkmark. function BenillaReputationAtWarBox_OnClick(box) FactionToggleAtWar(GetSelectedFaction()) if box:GetChecked() then PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOn") else PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOff") end ReputationFrame_Update() end
function BenillaReputationInactiveBox_OnClick(box) if box:GetChecked() then PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOn") SetFactionInactive(GetSelectedFaction()) else PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOff") SetFactionActive(GetSelectedFaction()) end ReputationFrame_Update() end
function BenillaReputationMainScreenBox_OnClick(box) if box:GetChecked() then PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOn") SetWatchedFactionIndex(GetSelectedFaction()) else PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOff") SetWatchedFactionIndex(0) end ReputationWatchBar_Update() end
-- The window's wheel handler (this file's header comment, deviation 7). function BenillaReputationFrame_OnMouseWheel(delta) BenillaFauxScrollFrame_OnMouseWheel(getglobal("ReputationListScrollFrame"), delta) end
-- ── Lifecycle (ref-lua l.16-30) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── function ReputationFrame_OnLoad() local frame = this frame:RegisterEvent("UPDATE_FACTION") -- The repaint is wired in the scroll frame's own `<OnVerticalScroll>` below, which is -- where the reference's kit puts it (1860). end
function ReputationFrame_OnShow() ReputationFrame_Update() end
function ReputationFrame_OnEvent(event) if event == "UPDATE_FACTION" then if this:IsVisible() then ReputationFrame_Update() end end end
